To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a reduction in the reinforcement rate, (b) a shift from a variable-interval 60-sec schedule to a variable-interval schedule, (c) a shift to a differential reinforcement of low-rate schedule, (d) an increase in the interresponse-time requirement, and (e) a decrease in the number of reinforcement sources, can produce a U-shaped gradient.
the rate of reinforcement is a necessary and sufficient determinant of inhibitory control.

inhibitory stimulus control is obtained when the rates of reinforcement associated with a stimulus pair are unequal and that the gradient of inhibition is oriented in a direction opposite to that of the stimulus correlated with higher reinforcement rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of stimulus control which emphasizes the role of the stimulus and the response as a unit of analysis.
the effects of the rate of reinforcement and the effects of the schedule of reinforcement on inhibitory stimulus control.
the role of behavioral contrast in the generation of inhibitory stimulus controls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduction in the rate or reinforcement is a sufficient determinant for inhibitory stimulus control.

inhibitory stimulus control can be produced by any procedure that results in a reduction in the rates of responding during one of the stimuli correlated with a schedule of reinforcement, and a contrast in the rates of reinforcement during the other stimulus.
the reduction in the rate or reinforcement is the critical factor in the development of inhibitory stimulus effects, not the extinction of the behavior correlated with one stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a reduction in the relative rate of reinforcement is a determinant of inhibition about the correlated stimulus.

inhibitory stimulus control is obtained when the rate of reinforcement for one stimulus is reduced, relative to the rate of reinforcement of the other stimulus, in the context of a reduction in the overall rate of reinforcement.
a reduction in the overall rate of responding, correlated with a stimulus, is a sufficient determinant of inhibitory control of behavior about the stimulus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a reduction in the rates of reinforcement is a sufficient condition for inhibitory stimulus control about a stimulus. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2018 APA, all rights reserved)
a reduction in the reinforcement rate is sufficient to generate a post-discrimination U-shaped gradient of response inhibition. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2021 APA, all rights reserved)
inhibitory stimulus control is not an all-or-none process, but is a function of a gradient of inhibition about a stimulus. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
